title: Is my certificate late? Maharashtra RTS calculator
h1: Is my certificate late? Maharashtra Right to Services date calculator
description: Enter the date your Maharashtra income or domicile certificate application was received. See the due date and the last day to file a first appeal.
direct_answer: Enter the date your complete application was received. For a Maharashtra income or domicile certificate, the time limit is 15 days. The calculator shows the due date, the day a first appeal becomes possible, and the last day to file it. Every rule it uses is listed below with its source.

question.q: When can I appeal if my certificate is late?
question.a: In Maharashtra you can file a first appeal once the 15 day time limit has passed without the certificate or a written rejection. The appeal must be filed within 30 days of the limit running out. A late appeal can be admitted for sufficient cause, up to 90 days.

audience: For anyone in Maharashtra waiting on an income or domicile certificate.

blocks.title: How to use it
items: Pick the certificate you applied for.
Enter the date on your acknowledgement, when the complete application was received.
If you have already filed a first appeal, enter that date too.
Read your dates. Each line names the rule it comes from.

blocks.title: The rules the calculator uses
rows: 15 days from receipt of the complete application
RTS list on Aaple Sarkar; Act section 5(1)
Last day for a first appeal
30 days after the time limit runs out, or after you receive a rejection. Up to 90 days for sufficient cause
Within 30 days of the first appeal order, or after 45 days from the first appeal if there is no order
Within 60 days of the second appeal order

blocks.html: Calendar days. The Act does not say whether the days are working days, so the calculator counts calendar days. If your last day falls on a holiday, file early. This is a counting aid, not legal advice.

blocks.title: Read the full guide
blocks.html: Documents, fees and the appeal form are in the income certificate guide and the domicile certificate guide. For how time limits work in general, see certificate time limits in India.

faq.q: Does the calculator count working days?
faq.a: No. It counts calendar days, because the Act does not say the days are working days.
No. The dates stay in your browser. The page has no analytics.
